## New features
- **New from Template…** File › New from Template… starts a project from one of four starters, or from a template you saved. The starters are BS 4142 plant, CRTN residential, Padel courts and BS 5228 construction. Each sets up its periods: the BS 4142 7.2 reference intervals (1 h by day, 15 min at night, rated on their busiest interval), CRTN Day 07:00–23:00 and Night 23:00–07:00, or the BS 5228 ABC periods. It also sets receptor defaults and heights (BS 4142: 1.5 m by day, 4.0 m at night; CRTN: a 1.5 m / 4.0 m floor pair) and the operating hours new sources start with (padel 07:00–22:00; construction Mon–Fri 08:00–18:00, Sat 08:00–13:00). New contour sheets use SmartSmooth and a layout with client and consultant cards from your company profile. Templates set up structure only: no objects, maps or results. File › Save as Template… keeps the current project's setup, including these defaults, in your profile's templates folder.
- **Operating hours for each source.** Point, line and area sources and courts have operating hours: Always (the default, which matches earlier versions), a preset such as 07:00–19:00, or typed hours with optional days ("Mon–Fri 08:00–18:00; Sat 08:00–13:00", "22:00–02:00"). The share of each period inside the hours becomes an on-time, time-weighted. A period with clock times takes its operating hours over its length. A reference interval (1 h, 15 min, worst hour) takes its busiest interval inside its window. With days given, the busiest operating day decides. The hours are their own named correction ("Operating hours 07:00–19:00: 12 of 16 h, −1.2 dB") in the calculation trace and in Why this level?, before the on-time. A percentage on-time then applies while the source operates. Set the hours in the Inspector or in the Inputs table. Several selected sources are set in one undo step.
- **A receptor height for each period.** A receptor can have its own height in a period, for example 1.5 m by day and 4.0 m at a first-floor bedroom window at night. That period is calculated at that height. The Inspector shows a height per period (blank uses the receptor's height). Results add a Height column ("Day 1.5 m · Night 4.0 m") when any receptor has one, and each level's tooltip gives the height it was calculated at. Receptors without period heights are unchanged.
- **Inputs, edited like a spreadsheet.** Edit name, height, level, group, operating hours, X/Y of point objects and Calculate in place. A level can be edited when it is the input itself (broadband, manual, the same in every period). Cmd+D fills the first selected cell down the selection. Cmd+C copies cells. Cmd+V pastes a block copied from Excel over several rows. Each of these is one undo step, and cells that cannot take a value are named in place. Paste Receptors makes receptors from rows of name, X, Y and height, in local metres or OSGB easting/northing (recognised, or say Local/OSGB in a fifth column), as one undo step.
- **Typed placement in the Inspector.** A point source, receptor or ground point takes X and Y typed in model metres or, when the project is georeferenced, as OSGB E/N (Local | OSGB E/N switch). The switch is hidden when the project has no georeference.
- **Linked selection.** Selecting a receptor or any object in Results, Inputs, the 3D view or on a contour sheet selects it in the Editor, and selecting in the Editor highlights its row in Results and Inputs and the object in 3D. A workspace that is not on screen catches up when you open it, so selecting everything in a large model stays as quick as before.
- **Show in Editor.** Right-click a Results row and choose Show in Editor, or Command-click the row or a marker on a contour sheet: AURIS switches to the Editor, selects the object and brings it into view.
- **What changed since this result?** The out-of-date chip in the status bar (click its label), the Results banner and the Contours banner now open a list of the edits made since the result was calculated, grouped by kind: object, field, and old → new value, from the model saved with the run. Names, colours and labels are left out because they do not change a level. Each object has Reveal, and Recalculate affected brings the result up to date. The list is cached per result and edit (about 60 ms the first time on a 300-building model). For contours calculated in an earlier session, the comparison is with the latest receptor calculation, and the list says so.
- **Tools menu.** Every drawing tool is listed with its single-key shortcut (V Select, H Pan, P Point source, B Building, ⇧B Noise barrier and the rest).
- **Object menu.** Combine and Subtract buildings, Auto place receptors and Merge roads have moved here from Edit › Select.
- **Keyboard focus halo.** When you move focus with the keyboard, a soft teal glow shows around the focused button, segmented control, field or toolbar tile. It is a blur outside the control, not an outline, and it goes away at the next click.
- **Name the source in the band editor.** Frequency bands now open with the source's name at the top (for example "Honda EU10i generator" or a condenser's make and model). Apply renames the source, and a Notes field holds the measurement position and height, operating condition and meter. Notes are kept with the source and saved to My library whatever the quantity. Bands, quantity, name and notes are one undo step.
- **Bars and levels as one object.** Each band has a bar with its level directly beneath. Thirds are bracketed into octaves, with the octave's energetic sum shown once. A dot marks an octave with only some thirds entered, and bands outside the ISO 9613-2 range are muted. Hover a bar to see the entered, A-weighted and derived sound power levels, or click it to edit that band. Editing a level eases its bar to the new height (immediate under Reduce Motion).
- **Faster band entry.** ⌥↑ and ⌥↓ change a level by 1 dB (with ⇧, 0.1 dB). Right-click a band to clear it or its octave. In 1/1 octave, a quiet second row shows each band A-weighted, or as sound power when the bands are sound pressure.
- **Calibrate a source to a measurement.** For point and area sources (Inspector › Calibration, or Project › Calibrate Source to Measurement…), enter a measured LAeq or octave-band Leq at a receptor or a point. AURIS solves the sound power so the model reproduces the measurement through its own receptor calculation, with the project's ground, terrain, screening and reflections; it does not use a closed-form Lp → Lw conversion. This avoids counting the radiation factor Q and the ground reflection twice. For broadband levels the solve finds one value; for octave bands it finds one value per band. The dialog shows the solved sound power, the model's band response and the residual (within 0.1 dB; normally under 0.01 dB). Nothing changes until you choose Apply, which is one undo step. Per-period sound powers move by the same amount, and on-times are left alone. The source keeps the calibration record (position, measured values, period, date, method). The Inspector reports the calibration out of date when the buildings, barriers, ground, terrain, propagation settings, method, source geometry, measurement position or the sound power itself change, and Re-solve runs it again. AURIS warns when the measurement was closer than twice the source's largest dimension (ISO 9613-2 Clause 4, raster factor k = 0.5). Proposed mitigation is left out of the solve, because a measurement describes the site as it is.
- **Field edit state.** A field you are typing in shows a soft amber outline as soon as its value differs from the saved one. Press Enter or click away and the outline eases to teal, then fades after about a second; Escape puts the saved value back. A value the field cannot take shows red. Values the app fills in itself never show amber. Applies to every text and number field, and is instant with Reduce Motion.
- **Stepping with modifier keys.** Every − / + key, spin-box arrow and the Up/Down keys in those fields step by 1 with a click, by 5 with Shift and by 0.1 with ⌘. Whole-number fields such as Bands step by 1 with ⌘. Fields that step in other units (5 % opacity, 0.1 m heights) scale the same way. Limits and decimals are kept, and the tooltip shows the steps.
- **Delete, Select All and clipboard keys in other workspaces.** When the macOS menu bar handles these keys outside the Editor, they now go to the table or view you are in. Delete in a Results or Inputs table can no longer remove plan objects you cannot see.
- **Side panel scroll position.** Pressing Enter in a field, or clicking away from it, no longer scrolls the Inspector (objects and Project) to another place. The field you committed stays where it was, even when rows above it appear or disappear. The Contours sheet panel, 3D side panel and Settings behave the same way.

## Changes
- **Inputs table layout.** Objects are grouped by type under headers that stay in view while scrolling. Rows highlight on hover. Clicking a column header sorts by it and shows the direction; a third click returns to placement order. Columns are chosen per type (Columns, or right-click a header) and remembered. Summaries are in plain words ("LpA 49.7 dB at 4.5 m", "LwA 80.0 dB/m", "1,200 vehicles (18 h)") instead of "Mode lp10". Heights and coordinates show 2 decimals, levels 1, lengths 1 and areas 0. Receptors show "—" in Calculate (they are always calculated). The table refreshes by itself, so the Refresh button is gone.
- **New from Template is a dialog** listing the starters and your templates, with what each sets up. It replaces the submenu.
- **On-time label.** When a source has operating hours, "% of time slice" reads "% of operating time".
- **Menus are back in the macOS menu bar.** You can search menu commands from Help, and Services, Full Screen and VoiceOver menu navigation work. Preferences…, About AURIS, Check for Updates… and Quit are in the AURIS menu. A new Window menu holds Minimise (⌘M), Zoom, Enter Full Screen (⌃⌘F) and Close Window (⌘W). Revert To now sits next to Save, and Project Settings… appears once, in Project. There are no blank first rows. Settings › General › Menus can put the menus back in the window.
- **Developer commands are hidden.** Show Splash and Force Refresh 3D View appear only when Settings › General › Developer commands is on.
- **"Period" everywhere.** The top bar says Period instead of Slice. Project › Time Slices… is now Periods…, and the period editor, inspector ("Include in Night"), road panel, sheet title block and dialogs all use "period". Project files and their saved keys are unchanged.
- **One Period and Scenario control.** The top bar's Period and Scenario always show a chevron, even with one choice. Results no longer has its own scenario chooser: a This scenario / All scenarios switch compares scenarios. The Project panel's preset is now labelled "Periods calculated", which sets which periods are calculated, not the one shown.
- **VoiceOver names.** The basemap adjustments button, empty-state artwork and segmented-control buttons now have proper names. The top bar's Period and Scenario are labelled by their captions.
- **The frequency band editor, rebuilt.** One calm surface, top to bottom: the name, the measurement as one sentence of controls ("Sound pressure at 3.5 m, 1.5 m high, Q = 2, Z-weighted"), the notes, the spectrum, and one prominent result (LwA) with a quiet secondary line (LpA at the distance, LwZ, and the ISO-range figure only when it differs). Explanations of distance, Q, Agr, output weighting and energy outside the ISO range moved into small ⓘ popovers and a "How AURIS uses this" link. The status line appears only when there is something to say: a band that needs attention, a paste result, or ISO octaves with no data. Apply, Cancel, Clear and Paste data sit in one footer, and Add to My library is a quiet action beside the name. Its card asks only for the category and data source, because the name and notes are already on the dialog. Calculated levels are unchanged.
- Source calibrations are saved with the project only when present, so other projects' files are unchanged. Calculated levels are unchanged.

## Bug fixes
- **No error card when editing assessment inputs.** Changing a BS 4142 background or another assessment input showed "'AurisComboBox' object is not callable" each time the change was committed in 0.57.0. The change itself was always saved and undoable.
- **Inspector focus.** Clicking a field while the previous field commits no longer hands focus to another field during the inspector's nested refresh.

## New features
- **Low frequency (NANR45) on the Internal tab.** When the model has third-octave source data, Results › Internal shows a quiet "Low frequency (NANR45)" card; Assess opens it. It compares a receptor's internal one-third-octave Leq from 10 Hz to 160 Hz with the NANR45 criterion curve (Defra, Revision 1, December 2011, Table 2), with the 5 dB relaxations for noise that occurs only during the day (Section 4.1) and for steady noise (Section 4.2). A band exceeds the curve when its internal level is above it; the card gives the margin in every band, the worst band and a plain-English summary, and notes that a sound up to about 5 dB below the curve may still be audible (Section 4.2).
- **Internal levels from a window reduction.** Internal = external − reduction: 13 dB in every band by default (a partially open window), editable for the project or one receptor, or entered per band from test data.
- **Measured levels for complaint investigations.** Levels can be predicted, or measured inside or outside: type or paste a row of third-octave Leq into the table (blank bands are not assessed). Measured exceedances in the 50 Hz band or from 80 Hz to 160 Hz carry the Section 4.2 notes on fridges and traffic.
- **Charts and tables for reports.** Copy chart puts a 300 dpi chart on white (receptor, period, assumptions footnote, exceedances in red with their margin) on the clipboard for Word; Save chart writes PNG, SVG or PDF; Copy table pastes as a Word table. Settings are saved with the project, and every change is an undo step.
- **Assessment readiness.** The report basis and Results now list what the assessments still need, apart from whether the calculation is within the validated software scope. The list covers missing BS 4142 backgrounds or BS 5228 ambients for an assessed period, and BS 4142 outcomes within 3 dB of a category boundary while broadband sources use the 500 Hz estimate. It also flags receptors with sources more than 1 km away, which is beyond ISO 9613-2 Table 4. Mixed sound-field bases within one assessment are flagged, as are bases the standard does not expect (BS 4142 free field; BS 5228 ABC façade). So are BS 8233 criteria compared with periods other than 16 h by day or 8 h at night, CRTN night levels that equal the day because only the 18-hour flow is entered, and roads with traffic but 0 % heavy vehicles. Calculated levels are unchanged.
- **Copy table for Word (BS 4142).** Results › BS 4142 copies the assessment in report layout: receptor, period with its reference interval, specific sound level LAeq,Tr, each character correction, rating level LAr,Tr, background LA90,T, the excess of the rating over the background, sound field and the Clause 11 initial estimate. It pastes into Word as a real table, and into a spreadsheet as tab-separated text.
- **Exclude from assessment.** Right-click a receptor in Results to exclude it from assessment, for example a measurement position. It is still calculated and listed, but it is left out of the summaries, counts, readiness and the Word table, and named in a note below the table. Undo reverts it.
- **Sound-field conversion, by choice.** BS 4142 can assess Façade receptors at their level less 3 dB, and BS 5228 can assess Free field receptors at their level plus 3 dB. Both are off by default. Assessment tables now show each receptor's sound field.
- **Draw, then edit.** When you place or finish an object, it is selected and the side panel switches to the Inspector. Esc cancels a shape you are drawing, and a second Esc returns to Select.
- **Assessment inputs in Undo.** BS 4142 backgrounds, corrections and background basis, pasted or typed values for single receptors, Internal (BS 8233), maximum-level and BS 5228 inputs are now named undo steps. Typing a value is one step.

## Changes
- **BS 4142 outcomes in the standard's words.** Initial estimates read "Indication of a significant adverse impact", "Indication of an adverse impact" or "Indication of a low impact", each "depending on the context" in exports. A rating above the background by less than 5 dB is no longer labelled "Low to adverse": it reads "Above background, below +5 dB". Outcomes are classified on the difference as shown (0.1 dB), so +4.96 dB shows as +5.0 dB and is classed at +5.0 dB. The basis sheet states this rounding rule.
- **BS 5228 ABC as Table E.1 reads.** The ambient is rounded to the nearest 5 dB once, for every category. Above the C value, an effect is significant only when the site raises the total by more than 3 dB, so exactly +3.0 dB is not significant. Site levels are judged as shown.
- **Corrected citations.** BS 4142 character corrections are cited as the subjective method (9.2). The 45 dB LAFmax night guideline is attributed to WHO (1999) and ProPG (2017), not BS 8233.
- **"Within validated software scope".** The report basis status no longer says "Ready for client-facing reporting". The status describes the software scope only, and the separate Assessment readiness list covers the assessment.
- **The metric is named everywhere.** Results column headers, the Excel and clipboard headers, the assessment columns and basis sheets show the metric and clock times, for example "LAeq,16h 07:00–23:00". CRTN on the Q18 basis shows "LA10,18h 06:00–24:00". The sheet title block and the default legend heading show the metric too, and the summary line no longer reads "· dB".
- **Copy Table copies what you see.** Only the columns on screen are copied. Excel exports still include every column.
- **One way to say "out of date".** The status chip, the Results and Contours banners, the inspector, Inputs and the 3D façade panel all say results are out of date because the model has changed, and they all offer **Recalculate** ("Recalculate all" for several results). The Results banner has its own Recalculate button. The validated-scope line is hidden while results are out of date.
- **Clearer CRTN night and heavy-vehicle inputs.** The TRL (2006) conversion option now says it uses TRL Method 3 for night. The road inspector notes when the night level follows the 18-hour flow (so night equals day) and when heavy vehicles are 0 % on a road with traffic. Defaults and calculated levels are unchanged.
- **Sound field label.** "Existing convention" now reads "Method convention".
- **Third-octave levels below 50 Hz are labelled as an extension.** ISO 9613-2 gives attenuation from the 63 Hz octave. In the NANR45 card each third-octave band from 50 Hz to 160 Hz takes its parent octave's attenuation; 10 Hz to 40 Hz use the 63 Hz octave's terms (divergence, ground, screening and the rest) with no atmospheric absorption. This is stated in the card, the calculation trace and the chart footnote, together with NANR45's own caution (Section 1.1) that it is not a prediction method. Calculated receptor levels and contours are unchanged.

## Bug fixes
- **An unchanged project no longer reopens out of date.** The last typed value kept for each manual input mode no longer counts as a model change, and results saved by an earlier AURIS are checked again against their own saved inputs. P2011 reopened after the update now shows current results.
- **Saved runs keep their calculation identity across updates.** A run's calculation identity now covers only the calculation modules and the release-gate golden results, so an update that changes only the interface or the engine's plumbing still lets saved runs show their path details. The full source digest is still recorded with each run, for information.

## New features
- **A new frequency band editor.** Third-octave bands now run from 6.3 Hz to 20 kHz. They sit in threes under their octave, and the octave, the broadband dB(A) and dB(Z) totals and a small chart update as you type. Switch between 1/3 and 1/1 octave entry, paste a row or column from Excel or Numbers, and move between cells with Tab, Return or the arrow keys.
- **Blank bands mean "no data".** A band left empty is not treated as 0 dB. An octave with some thirds missing shows the sum of what you entered and is marked "2 of 3". Energy outside the 63 Hz–8 kHz range that ISO 9613-2 propagates is reported in dB(A) rather than dropped silently.
- **Measured band levels.** Bands can be entered as sound pressure at a distance, with the directivity Q (1 free field, 2 on a reflecting plane, 4 at a wall–ground junction, 8 in a corner). AURIS shows the sound power it derives, band by band. A short note explains when Q = 2 would count the ground reflection twice with ISO 9613-2.
- **My library.** Your own source records now live in My library, separate from the read-only AURIS library and shared across all your projects. "Add to My library" in the inspector and the band editor saves the current source in one click: name, category, sound power or measured sound pressure with distance, Q and height, bands, weighting, notes and data source. The library browser switches between My library, AURIS and All, with search, categories, a details panel showing where each record came from, Duplicate to My library for AURIS records, and Undo after deleting your own. Import and export My library as JSON or CSV to share records with colleagues.
- **Library records travel with the project.** A source using one of your records keeps a copy in the project, so it opens and calculates the same on another Mac, where it is marked "In this project" and can be added to that Mac's My library in one click.
- **Delete a basemap from its list.** With the basemap list open, hold Shift and press and hold a map for about a second to delete it, then Undo within a few seconds if needed. A deleted map is removed from the project, every sheet, the 3D view, the undo history and the image caches on disk.

## Changes
- **Existing library records move into My library** on first use, unchanged, with a dated backup of the old file. An older record measured as sound pressure without a recorded distance or Q now asks for them once, instead of assuming 10 m and Q = 1.
- **Inspector sections open and close smoothly**, and the Project panel lines up with the inspector.
- **Unweighted bands by default.** New spectra are entered as Z (unweighted), as most sound level meters export them. Existing spectra keep the weighting they were saved with. The editor states that the model reports dB(A) and that unweighted bands are A-weighted after propagation.
- **One clear source level.** Level from is Broadband, 1/1 octave, 1/3 octave or Library. With band or library data, the broadband level is shown read-only as the value derived from it. Clicking it offers to switch to a broadband level instead, keeping the bands so you can switch back. Resulting sound power spells out the arithmetic, for example "54.7 entered + 25.1 dB scenario correction = 79.8 used in the calculation".
- **Older projects whose entered level and band data disagree** open unchanged with a short notice explaining which level is used, and one-click ways to resolve it.
- **A tidier inspector.** The object type and name sit on one line with a soft status pill, the band editor opens from a labelled "Edit bands…" button, and position reads "X −22.86 m". The header lines up with every field below it.
- **A lighter basemap bar.** The A/B layer badge is one clean letter that rolls when you switch layers. The link icon on the Contours and 3D tabs is larger and clearer.
- **A redesigned basemap layer panel.** Opacity, brightness and contrast have editable values, there is a Colour | Black & white switch, a Blend list, and Offset (m) fields that fit. Reset is a quiet text action.
- **Clearer icons.** The terrain contour line tool shares the terrain point's yellow. The receptor icon is a plain blue tile, and the toolbar gains a noise-barrier glyph. Each tool plays a short motion when chosen, and neutral glyphs follow dark mode.
- **Cleaner contour edges.** Contours near foliage areas and building shadows follow the calculated field more closely: the area drawn in the wrong band roughly halves on the projects tested, and calculated levels are unchanged. Long straight band edges along foliage areas and shadow lines are real steps in the ISO 9613-2 levels (the Annex A foliage attenuation starts at a 10 m path through foliage).
- **A smaller download.** About 250 MB of stale development caches are no longer packed into the app.

## Bug fixes
- **Results and exports show each receptor's own ID.** They renumbered locations as REC_001, REC_002…, so REC_003's level could appear under "REC_002". Plan and sheet markers keep their numbers.
- **Switching between sound power and sound pressure** while band data was in use restored an older typed level and silently rescaled the spectrum.
- **Export Diagnostics no longer includes map provider keys** (Google keys were included in clear text), and the settings file is readable by your account only.
- **Saving keeps a project file's permissions.** Every save made the file readable by its owner only, which broke shared folders and network drives.
- **The Smoothness setting no longer pulls contours into points** at the edge of a building's shadow.

## New features
- **BS 4142 backgrounds for day, night and operational hours.** Results › BS 4142 has three background sound levels (LA90): Day, Night and Operational hours. Each period refers to one of them (night periods to Night, day periods to Day, an assessment period or worst hour to Operational hours, a single clock hour by its time), and "Period uses" lets you choose another for any period. Background levels for individual receptors still work. The separate BS 4142 period type is gone: use the normal periods. Older projects keep their BS 4142 periods and background values.
- **A BS 4142 colour scheme for contours.** The palette "BS 4142: rating level against background" colours the rating level against the period's background: light green 10 dB or more below, green below background, amber up to 5 dB above, and red from 5 dB above (adverse impact likely; significant from +10 dB). Character corrections are included, and the bands follow the background when you change it.
- **Update all.** When several results are out of date, the status chip reads "N results out of date · Update all" and reruns them one after another; Stop ends the whole run.
- **Keyboard shortcuts at a glance.** ⌘/ (or Help › Keyboard Shortcuts) shows every shortcut and mouse gesture, grouped and searchable.
- **An example project.** "…or open the example" on the start card (also in Help) opens a small demo site as an untitled copy to try things out on.
- **Measurements while you draw.** A small readout beside the cursor shows the segment length and bearing, the total length and the area while you draw, both sides and the area of a building rectangle, and the distance and bearing while you move a selection. Type a length and press Return to fix the segment.
- **Undo you can read.** Undo steps are named after what changed ("Add 3 receptors", "Move building"), Edit › Undo and Redo say what they will do, and Edit › History jumps back or forward several steps at once.
- **Revert to an earlier save.** File › Revert To… lists the last saves ("Today 14:32") and restores one; the current file is kept as a backup.

## Changes
- **"Out of date" only when results would change.** Results are marked out of date only when an edit can change a level: geometry, heights, sources and traffic, receptors, terrain, ground, periods or calculation settings. Renaming, recolouring, labels, glyphs, sheet styling and app updates no longer do, and undoing an edit makes results current again.
- **Consistent export names.** Every export suggests "project number - item - 01" (for example "P2000 - Contours - 03.pdf", "P2000 - 3D View - 01.png", "P2000 - Results - 01.xlsx") in the project's last export folder. The number counts on from what is already there and you can change it before saving.
- **Calmer foliage on plans and sheets.** Tree symbols take the area's own green at a lower strength, more widely spaced and a little smaller, so contour maps no longer look busy.
- **Trees in 3D in a deliberate model style.** Clean, softly shaded canopies that are lighter on top, a shape for each species (three more: field maple, horse chestnut and yew), crisp clipped hedges with lighter tops, and detail that crossfades with distance instead of popping.
- **Bridges meet their approaches in 3D.** The road eases off a bridge deck into the approach without a step or fold, and concrete abutments close deck ends that stand above the ground. Calculation heights are unchanged.
- **Smoother 3D ground.** Survey facets are rounded (never more than 5 cm from the calculated ground); kerbs, road edges and banks stay exact, and banks no longer show light and dark wedges under a low sun.
- **A clearer Façades button.** The 3D toolbar's Façades glyph is now a building with windows.
- **Much faster on big projects.** Selecting all buildings on P2000 takes 0.25 s instead of 15 s (5,000 buildings: under half a second instead of minutes), the Contours tab first opens in 1.7 s instead of 6.7 s and returns in 0.2 s, and Settings › Performance opens at once.
- **More room on the splash and update screens.** The progress bar sits further from the text above it.
- **Broadband sources say how they were calculated.** For a source with only an A-weighted sound power, ISO 9613-2:2024 (Clause 1) estimates attenuation from the 500 Hz terms. The receptor trace, the protocol export, the report basis and the readiness notes now say so, and give the path's own range of ground attenuation across the bands (from the geometry only), so you can see when 500 Hz is the band with the most ground attenuation and the estimate may read low. Supplying octave-band data gives a full spectral calculation. Calculated levels are unchanged.
- **A notice for sources drawn inside a building.** Readiness notes now point out a point source inside a drawn building, which that building screens; useful when a source level was calibrated from a measurement outside the building.
- **Calm error notices.** If something unexpected goes wrong, a small card says what failed and that nothing was lost, with Copy details for support, instead of a dialog.
- **Settings › Preferences.** The machine-wide settings are called Preferences everywhere (they were "Global" in Settings).
- **The installer shows the AURIS icon** on the mounted disk again.

## Bug fixes
- **Tree and building symbols stay inside the map frame** on sheets and exports; they no longer spill into the margin over the grid labels. Large foliage areas also draw much faster on sheets.
- **Typing goes into the field you clicked.** In the inspector, clicking a field such as On time or LAFmax right after editing another one sent your typing into the source's Height field.
- **Save after Save As keeps your file name.** The next ⌘S no longer renamed the file after the project name.
- **A self-crossing area source** is caught before calculating with a plain message and Locate, instead of an error.
- **The status chip no longer says "Saved"** for a while after an edit.
- **View › Frame All** frames the model instead of jumping to the origin.
- **The receptor trace shows the source-position correction (DΩ) of the A-weighted ground method** as its own term; it appeared as "Reflections +3.0 dB" in the level breakdown. Broadband sources no longer always show "Reflections 0" in the trace and protocol export.
- **Two saves within a second** both keep a backup.

## New features
- **Works calmly offline.** When the update check finds no internet, a small notice says you're offline and that AURIS will check again once you're connected; it then looks quietly and tells you only if there is an update. Choose "No thanks, I'll check myself" or turn it off in Settings › Updates › Check when back online. Map, terrain and basemap imports say plainly when the Mac is offline, and data already imported keeps working.
- **A solid 3D north arrow.** The 3D view's north arrow keeps the sheet's upright ring and N, and its needle is now a small lit, ridged solid (dark north, light south) that turns and leans with the camera, the same in copied and saved views, Ultra renders and videos.
- **Go to View for renders.** The render window's Go to View (also on each recent render's menu) moves the 3D view back to the camera that render was taken from.
- **Tilt-shift to taste.** The tilt-shift blur now reaches a light touch as well as the miniature look, and its amount is in Settings › 3D view.

## Changes

## Changes
- **Day, evening and night are calculated together.** Propagation does not change between periods, only the sources' levels do, so each source-to-receptor path is now solved once and reused for every period, with identical results: a three-period receptor run with lines and roads took 5 s instead of 18 s.
- **Large models no longer run out of memory.** A 1,000-building model with 20 roads used over 9 GB while calculating receptors (enough to stall a Mac); it now peaks at 4 GB, with the same levels. Building the visibility between obstacles for lateral paths is twice as fast on such models.
- **Small and medium receptor calculations are several times faster.** Calculations run inside the window were collecting profiling detail for every source-receiver path, which kept them off the compiled solver. They no longer do; results are identical (62 validation scenarios: 10 s to 1.5 s).
- **The plan is smoother on large models.** On a 5,000-building model, the pointer's hover and pick work takes 5 ms instead of 11 ms (picking a building edge 2 ms instead of 35 ms), and a zoomed-out redraw takes half as long (0.09 s instead of 0.18 s), so panning, zooming and hovering stay fluid.
- **The 3D view opens faster on large models.** Building foundations now sample the ground in one batch instead of point by point, and only the map tiles that hold pavement are cut around roads: a 1,000-building model with 20 roads and 1,000 receptors opens in 3D in 6.8 s instead of 13.9 s, and receptor and source markers are built twenty times faster. Editing one building rebuilds only that building's 3D shape (three times faster on 1,000 buildings).
- **Up to 10,000 sources, receptors, line sources and area sources of each kind** (was 512), for façade receptor grids and imported models.
- **SmartSmooth's Simplify keeps contours in place.** Simplify allowed each level to change by up to its dB tolerance, which in a weak far-field gradient let a line drift several metres (up to 3.9 m at the strongest setting on a test site). Now an even slope keeps its contours within a fraction of a grid cell, while bumps, dips and grid-scale wiggles are still smoothed away by the full tolerance. Against exact 0.25 m contours, lines are about twice as close at every Simplify and Smoothing setting (for example Simplify 4: 1.1 m instead of 2.4 m at the 95th percentile) and as smooth as before.
- **Smaller field steps are drawn as clean lines.** Calculate looked only for level steps of 0.3 dB or more. A smaller step matters when the level around it changes slowly (0.1 dB in a 0.1 dB/m far field moves a contour by a metre), and those are now found and proved too, down to 0.08 dB, so they no longer kink the contours.
- **Exported contours match the drawing.** GIS export (DXF, GeoPackage, Shapefile) now writes the contour lines the sheet shows (SmartSmooth, with its field-step lines), and a new **Contour bands** layer of filled band polygons with their range and label. Before, the lines were traced again from the raw grid, so they differed from the sheet and showed false rings around buildings.

- **A calculation could hang on a receptor or source with a coordinate that is not a number**, using all memory; it now stops with a message pointing to Model preflight.

## Bug fixes
- **Numbers on receptor markers and other labels could show holes** where a character's strokes cross (the 4 in particular). Lettering now keeps overlapping strokes.
- **AURIS could fill the disk with temporary calculation files.** Each calculation's worker processes kept a copy of the scene (tens of megabytes) for every batch of receivers until the calculation ended, and copies left by a crash or force-quit were never removed. Only the copies in use are kept now, and leftovers are removed when AURIS starts.
- **Contours could fail with "Failed in nopython mode pipeline … Known signatures".** Two things combined. After an update the app restarted with the previous version's settings for its calculation kernels, so every version since 0.41 kept using the 0.41 kernel folder: its own ready-compiled kernels were never installed, and each calculation compiled them again in all its worker processes at once. Workers compiling the same kernel at the same moment could then file one variant under another's name, and a later calculation picked up the wrong one and stopped. Each version now always uses its own kernel folder, and workers that compile at the same time no longer overwrite each other. First calculations after an update are also faster again, because the bundled kernels are used.
- **A crash when the main window's title bar was updated without the native Mac window system**, for example while the app was checked automatically without a display. The title bar now looks up the Mac window only on macOS's own window system.

  - **Simplify now states its accuracy.** Each step allows the drawn field to differ from the calculated levels by at most 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1 or 2 dB (Raw: none). Within that, it draws the smoothest contours possible. Features smaller than the allowance (spikes, needles, notches, stair-steps) go, and anything larger is kept.

  - **Smoothing follows the contours.** Close to a source, where contours are tight, smoothing reaches only a short way and they keep their shape. Far afield, where contours are wide apart, it reaches further, giving long, clean curves.
  - **Smooth curves, never stair-steps.** The calculated grid is interpolated with a smooth curve that never goes beyond its neighbouring points, and simplified contour lines lose the grid's stair-steps.
  - **Walls and barriers are exact.** Contours never pass through a building, barrier or court wall. Where the level jumps across a wall, the bands on each side run straight up to it, with no slivers or specks along the wall.
  - **Bands and lines always agree.** Every band boundary is a single shared line: no gaps, overlaps or crossings at any setting.

## Changes

- **What made the difference:** lateral paths round buildings (ISO 9613-2 7.4.3) are found with a much better-guided search that still returns the exact shortest route, and building visibility is worked out once instead of for every few receivers. Ground profiles are sampled only where the terrain could reach the ray, and refinement now uses every processor core to the end of each pass.
